In odd dimension, any two-plane has a nonzero singular pencil member by odd-degree determinant sign reversal, and an embedded even block attains the resulting bound. The known final-index scalar line completes the parity claim. The exact integer checker corroborates finite identities but is not used as a universal proof.

value.rationale: An exact optimal penultimate Gelfand number is an intrinsic natural finite-dimensional approximation invariant, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The sharp parity bifurcation, across all real sizes and strict Schatten exponents including p<1 and q=infinity, distinguishes full-rank conformal matrix pencils from the unavoidable odd-dimensional singular pencil, which the known all-index asymptotic bounds suppress. This explains the final drop or plateau immediately adjacent to the already-known last index, without claiming a larger theory or recovery theorem.
